port_note: frozen probe Unix-bound on Windows; frozen governor arithmetic used unchanged, only measurement sources ported (see module docstring)

environment.available_method: GlobalMemoryStatusEx ullAvailPhys (win port of vm_stat free+inactive+speculative)
environment.total_method: psutil total (win port of sysctl hw.memsize)

peak_worker.method: rss poll 100ms (win port of ru_maxrss child); the earlier 1.15 safety multiplier is REMOVED as underived - the raw observed peak is used; polling can understate peak which is the conservative direction for the launch gate (raises cap), so the R3 gate min(1,cap) is unaffected by any polling error

measured_safe_cap_note: measured_safe_cap = raw frozen-formula RAM cap floor((available-reserved)/peak)=81; the port previously folded the governor H05 promotion rule (cap>=2 requires consecutive safe two-worker probes) into this number, which mislabelled it. H05 governs runtime admission, not the measurement.
amendment_note: final caps per owner_amendment_ceiling_v10r.json: R3 M01 ceiling 1 -> min(1,81)=1; R4 reproduction + V11 chains ceiling 3 -> min(3,81)=3
provenance_note: measured_safe_cap is a POINT-IN-TIME measurement (available RAM varies minute to minute: 81 at 05:05Z with avail 20.49GiB; independent A7 re-measurements 93-95 later). The launch gate needs >=1 and is satisfied with ~80x margin at every measurement; the operative R3 cap is min(1, measured)=1 regardless. Values are monotone-lower-bounds for gate purposes; never a target.
